en.title: Eswatini Launches First Costed National Disability Plan; Global Accessibility Updates Follow
en.summary: Eswatini, with UNESCO, unveiled its first costed national disability plan for 2024‑2028, turning rights into funded action. Amazon released an adaptive display feature for Fire TV to improve living‑room accessibility, while the Organization of Asian Journalists introduced measures to make newsrooms more accessible. Meanwhile, an accessibility group criticized Metrolinx for what it calls the ‘world’s stupidest ramp,’ and a report shows avoidable deaths among people with learning disabilities remain double the general population.

highlights.title: Eswatini launches first Costed National Disability Plan
Amazon Launches Adaptive Display Feature for Fire TV to Create Accessible Living Room Experience
OAJ is making news and newsrooms more accessible
Accessibility group criticizes Metrolinx for 'stupidest ramp in the world'
Avoidable deaths fall but remain double for people with learning disabilities

zh-TW.title: 埃斯瓦蒂尼發布首個成本計算國家殘障計畫；多國無障礙動向更新
zh-TW.summary: 埃斯瓦蒂尼在聯合國教科文組織支持下，推出首個2024－2028年成本計算的國家殘障行動計畫，將殘障權利轉為有資金支持的具體行動。亞馬遜為Fire TV釋出適應性顯示功能，以提升客廳無障礙體驗；亞洲記者協會則推動新聞與新聞室更無障礙。此外，無障礙團體批評Metrolinx坡道設計不合理，而一篇討論ADHD與身心障礙意識的社群貼文引發關注。
